To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the most useful feature is the syntactic relation of the head noun, (ii) the next most useful features are the syntactic relation between the head nouns and their immediate modifiers, and (iii) the best results are obtained by a classifier that makes use of WordNet information

(a) the most effective features are the ones that capture the syntactic and semantic similarity of the two nouns in the relation, and (b) the most effective way to capture this similarity is by using the WordNet hierarchy.

(i) the best performance can be achieved by combining classifiers trained on different feature sets, (ii) a combination of classifiers trained on the same feature set but with and without Word-Net information is also useful, (iii) the best performance on the test set is obtained using a combination of classifiers that do not make use of any Word-Net information, and that (iv) the best performance is achieved by combining classifiers that use different feature selection algorithms
